subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 39 medium / 61 hard. Tier is relative: the hard third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: In children with cystic fibrosis, airway clearance should be performed:

options.A: Daily, with age-appropriate techniques, before meals or two hours after

questions.question: Complete (third-degree) heart block is characterised by:

options.A: Progressive PR lengthening then dropped beat only
options.C: A prolonged PR interval with all P waves conducted
options.D: Complete dissociation between atrial and ventricular activity with a slow ventricular rate

questions.explanation: Treated with a permanent pacemaker.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A displaced intracapsular femoral neck fracture in an elderly patient is best treated by:
questions.explanation: To permit early mobilisation.

questions.question: How is musculoskeletal (chest wall) pain typically distinguished from pleuritic pain on physical examination?

options.A: Musculoskeletal pain is reproduced by palpation, while pleuritic pain is not
options.B: Both are always identical and cannot be distinguished clinically
options.C: Pleuritic pain is always reproduced by palpation, musculoskeletal pain never is
options.D: Musculoskeletal pain never worsens with movement

questions.explanation: Musculoskeletal (chest wall) pain is usually well localized and its reproduction on palpation is a key distinguishing clinical feature — pleuritic pain, by contrast, is not reproduced by palpation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems

questions.question: A feature of overtraining syndrome is:

options.B: Very high frequency with sensory-only intensity

questions.question: In a wax bath, paraffin wax is commonly mixed with liquid paraffin (mineral oil) in the ratio:

questions.question: The Hawkins-Kennedy impingement test involves forward flexing the arm to 90° and then forcibly:

questions.explanation: CO binds haemoglobin with 200 times the affinity of oxygen.

questions.question: The posterior interosseous nerve passes through the:

questions.question: In an ERECT chest radiograph, the first and most important radiographic sign of elevated left ventricular pressure (early left ventricular failure) is:

options.A: Upper lobe blood diversion (shunting of blood to the upper zones)
options.B: A completely normal-appearing chest X-ray in all cases
options.C: Immediate cavitation of the lung fields

questions.explanation: As left atrial pressure rises, blood is shunted to the upper zones — upper lobe blood diversion — which is the first and most important radiographic sign of elevated left ventricular pressure on an erect film. This sign cannot be reliably assessed on a supine radiograph due to redistribution of blood flow in that position.
